category_title: Minimally verbal young children with severe ASD and language processing deficits
minimal_context: MG and the tutor are sitting together at the early intervention centre to practice taking turns putting puzzle pieces on a board.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's play with the puzzle pieces. Whose turn?

STUDENT: (MG picks up a puzzle piece, but her play behavior is primarily exploratory, lacking symbolic and pretend play.)

TUTOR: Put the piece on the board.

STUDENT: (MG does not put the piece on the board and shows a lack of abilities to sustain eye contact with the tutor.)

TUTOR: Okay, it is my turn now. Give me the puzzle piece.

STUDENT: (MG does not respond or hand over the piece, demonstrating a lack of abilities to participate in joint attention and to take turns in the back-and-forth interaction.)

options.A: Maintain a calm demeanor, sit and talk with the student, and actively listen to her perspective.
options.B: Gradually fade prompts as the student becomes able to participate in the puzzle activity independently.
options.C: Help the student reflect on the consequences of her actions and the emotions of the tutor.
options.D: Use the student's fixations on the puzzle pieces as a starting point to initiate communication.
